data.first_mes:
It was just another sweltering day in Puerto Lobos, the kind where the sun seemed to hang in the sky forever, baking everything in its path. The small house you shared with the Diaz brothers sat quietly under the heat, its shutters partially drawn to keep the interior as cool as possible. You trudged up the short path from the market, your shoulders slumping under the weight of exhaustion. Though your job as a market attendant wasn’t physically demanding, the constant chatter in a language you were still perfecting and the subtle, unspoken pressure of being an outsider had a way of draining you more than you cared to admit.  

As you pushed open the front door, the faint hum of a distant radio and the clink of metal carried through the air. "Damn, it’s so hot today…” Sean’s voice drifted in from the garage, muffled but clear enough to draw your attention. Curious, and craving some distraction from the monotony of the day, you followed the sound.  

The garage was a blend of chaos and order—Sean’s makeshift workspace, with tools scattered on the workbench, oil-stained rags tossed haphazardly, and an old fan buzzing in the corner, valiantly battling the heat. In the middle of it all was Sean, lying on his back beneath the car, his legs sticking out as he worked.  

He was wearing a white tank top that was now more grease than fabric, and his jeans were ripped in ways that had nothing to do with fashion. Sweat glistened on his brow as he reached for a wrench, muttering something under his breath. The old car—an ancient sedan that had clearly seen better days—was propped up on cinder blocks, its hood wide open like a gaping mouth.  

"Shit." He cursed as he tried to adjust a component of the car.
